reviewMetadata.sourceLessonFamily: Place Value, Powers of Ten, and Decimals

learnerMaterial.title: Read Decimals by Place Value
learnerMaterial.subject: mathematics
learnerMaterial.lessonGoal: Today you will read decimals through thousandths and connect each digit to its value. Decimal place value is useful when you measure and compare.
successCriteria: I can name tenths, hundredths, and thousandths.
I can write a decimal in word form and expanded form.
keyPoints: The decimal point separates whole-number places from decimal places.
Each place to the right is one tenth of the place to its left.

vocabulary.definition: one of 100 equal parts of a whole
one of 1,000 equal parts of a whole

sections.title: A decimal place-value chart
sections.body: Read 4.307 as four and three hundred seven thousandths.

sections.title: Worked example: unpack 2.645
sections.directions: The answer is shown because this is a worked example.

items.prompt: Write 2.645 in expanded form and word form.

steps: The 2 is in the ones place: 2.
The 6 is in the tenths place: 0.6.
The 4 is in the hundredths place: 0.04.
The 5 is in the thousandths place: 0.005.
Word form: two and six hundred forty-five thousandths.

sections.title: Your turn: name a digit's value

items.prompt: What is the value of the 8 in 6.082?

feedback.correct: You counted two places to the right of the decimal point: hundredths.
feedback.incorrect: Start just right of the decimal point with tenths, then count one place at a time.

feedback.correct: Your word form preserves the zero hundredths and names thousandths.
feedback.incorrect: Use “and” for the decimal point. Then read 409 and name the last place: thousandths.

items.prompt: Write 7.052 in expanded form. Explain what the zero tells you.

feedback.correct: You represented each nonzero digit and explained the empty tenths place.
feedback.incorrect: Place the digits in a chart first. The zero keeps the 5 in the hundredths place.

sections.title: Reteach: count from the decimal point
sections.body: Touch the decimal point. Move right: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. A zero can hold a place even when its value is zero.

items.prompt: Which decimal means five and six thousandths?

feedback.correct: You used zeros to hold the tenths and hundredths places.
feedback.incorrect: Six thousandths puts the 6 in the third place to the right of the decimal point.

items.prompt: Write 9.174 in word form and expanded form. Then name the value of the 7.

feedback.correct: All three representations agree, and the digit value matches its place.
feedback.incorrect: Check each position in a place-value chart, especially the hundredths place.

whatYouLearned: Tenths, hundredths, and thousandths are places right of the decimal point.
Zeros can hold places in a decimal.
Standard, word, and expanded forms must show the same value.
